To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Cu wire tail picks up Au material, and the Au residue in the FAB reduces the hardness of the Cu wire bond.
the hardness of a Cu FAB can be influenced by Au pick up, but only if the Au pick up is high enough.
Cu pick up on the substrate surface during wire bonding leads to an increase of the free air ball (50 μmm diameter) hardness of 1.2 HV to 4.3 HV, depending on the amount of Au pick-up.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of substrate material pick on the hardness of Cu wire free air balls.
the effect of substrate material (Au) pick up on the Cu wire tail during FAB formation.
the influence of substrate material pick-up by the wire tail on the Cu FABs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Au pick up by the tail of a Cu wire bond has a significant influence on the mechanical properties of the subsequently formed Cu FAB.
Cu free air ball hardness can be influenced by the amount of substrate pick up, but the effect is small.
Au pick up does not influence the hardness of the FAB significantly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hardness of the FAB is influenced by the pick up of substrate material.
Au pick up is found to have a significant effect on the Cu wire tail and subsequently formed FAB.
Cu free air ball hardness is strongly influenced by Au pick up from the substrate metallization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hardness of the FAB can vary strongly due to the presence of substrate pick up.
the hardness of the FAB can be influenced by pick up of the substrate material.
Cu wire tail pick up can be significant and should be considered when evaluating Cu FAB hardness.
